uncited: *   Training views: A set of images $I$ with corresponding camera poses.
*   **Active Set ($A$):** A boolean mask or index list identifying which Gaussians are currently being optimized.
*   **Non-Active Set ($\bar{A}$):** The complement of $A$, containing Gaussians that are frozen.
*   **Pre-rendered Images ($I^{pre}$):** A buffer storing the rendered contribution of the non-active set $\bar{A}$ for each training view.
**Initialization:** Initialize the active set $A$ to include all Gaussians.
Initialize pre-rendered images $I^{pre}$ for all training views.
**Rasterize Active Gaussians:** Render only the Gaussians in the active set $G_A$ using the pre-rendered image $I_i^{pre}$ as the background/base.
**Lazy Pre-rendered Image Update:** When a Gaussian $i$ moves from $A$ to $\bar{A}$ (becomes inactive), its contribution must be added to the pre-rendered images.
This allows the initial densification phase of 3DGS to complete before sparsity optimization begins.
*   **Pre-rendered Image Update Cost:** Directly updating all pre-rendered images after each active set update is prohibitive due to sparsity and poor GPU parallelism.

*   **Active Set Update Complexity:** Naively updating the active set by re-evaluating gradients of all Gaussians for all views has complexity comparable to a full-variable update, negating acceleration.
*   **Variance:** The method exhibits noticeable variance across different runs due to the stochastic nature of subsampling and farthest point sampling.
*   **Time Complexity:** The training time is reduced by a factor proportional to the sparsity of the active set.
*   **Memory Complexity:** Memory usage is similar to standard OIT-based 3DGS, requiring storage for pre-rendered images for each training view.
Accelerates training by freezing converged Gaussians.
Requires careful tuning of the activation threshold $\epsilon_v$ and the update interval.
The Active Set Method for OIT-based 3DGS, also known as SparseOIT, was proposed to address the computational inefficiencies of Order-Independent Transparency (OIT) based 3D Gaussian Splatting.
Standard 3DGS relies on depth sorting, which is expensive.
OIT-based methods remove sorting but suffer from slower convergence and higher computational cost due to the lack of sparsity exploitation.
